From c9520be3839063bbb50aabec531cc0d0b8595564 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Maxime Ripard <maxime.ripard@free-electrons.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jan 2017 23:41:56 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] clk: sunxi-ng: mult: Fix minimum in round rate

The previous code was always taking 1 as the minimum in it's round_rate
function, ignoring entirely what was set as minimum in the clock
definition.

Make sure that's not the case anymore.

Fixes: 2beaa601c849 ("clk: sunxi-ng: Implement minimum for multipliers")
Acked-by: Chen-Yu Tsai <wens@csie.org>
Signed-off-by: Maxime Ripard <maxime.ripard@free-electrons.com>

diff --git a/drivers/clk/sunxi-ng/ccu_mult.c b/drivers/clk/sunxi-ng/ccu_mult.c
index 8b7ee7baa85b..a52162195e07 100644
--- a/drivers/clk/sunxi-ng/ccu_mult.c
+++ b/drivers/clk/sunxi-ng/ccu_mult.c
@@ -40,7 +40,7 @@ static unsigned long ccu_mult_round_rate(struct ccu_mux_internal *mux,
 	struct ccu_mult *cm = data;
 	struct _ccu_mult _cm;
 
-	_cm.min = 1;
+	_cm.min = cm->mult.min;
 	_cm.max = 1 << cm->mult.width;
 	ccu_mult_find_best(parent_rate, rate, &_cm);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/clk/sunxi-ng/ccu_mult.c`**
- The line that previously set the minimum value for the `_cm` structure to `1` has been changed. 
- The new code now sets `_cm.min` to `cm->mult.min`, which retrieves the minimum value defined in the clock configuration instead of hardcoding it to `1`.

### Relationships
- The modification in `ccu_mult.c` addresses a bug where the minimum rate for the clock multiplier was incorrectly fixed at `1`, disregarding any user-defined minimum values. By updating this line, the patch ensures that the clock multiplier respects the defined minimum rate, thus fixing the issue introduced in a previous commit (identified by the hash `2beaa601c849`). This change enhances the functionality of the clock multiplier by allowing it to operate within the specified limits.

Here is the commit message:
clk: sunxi-ng: mult: Fix minimum in round rate

The previous code was always taking 1 as the minimum in it's round_rate
function, ignoring entirely what was set as minimum in the clock
definition.

Make sure that's not the case anymore.

Fixes: 2beaa601c849 ("clk: sunxi-ng: Implement minimum for multipliers")
Acked-by: Chen-Yu Tsai <wens@csie.org>
Signed-off-by: Maxime Ripard <maxime.ripard@free-electrons.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `ccu_mult_round_rate` function always setting the minimum rate to a hardcoded value of `1`, which ignored the user-defined minimum value specified in the clock configuration. This led to incorrect behavior when attempting to round the clock rate, as it did not take into account the actual constraints defined for the clock multiplier.

Here is the patch:
 
 static unsigned long ccu_mult_round_rate(struct ccu_mux_internal *mux,
 					unsigned long parent_rate,
 					unsigned long rate,
 					void *data)
 {
 	struct ccu_mult *cm = data;
 	struct _ccu_mult _cm;
 
-	_cm.min = 1;
+	_cm.min = cm->mult.min;
 	_cm.max = 1 << cm->mult.width;
 	ccu_mult_find_best(parent_rate, rate, &_cm);
 
 	return parent_rate * _cm.mult;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
_cm.min = 1;
```
Reason:
This line hardcodes the minimum rate to `1`, completely disregarding any user-defined minimum value specified in the clock configuration. As a result, the function does not respect the actual constraints for the clock multiplier, leading to incorrect rounding behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
_cm.min = cm->mult.min;
```
Reason:
This line updates the minimum rate to use the user-defined minimum value from the clock configuration (`cm->mult.min`). By doing so, it ensures that the rounding function respects the defined constraints, allowing for correct behavior when rounding the clock rate.
